subject: English Language
text: Each of the students ____ the assignment before the deadline.
explanation: With 'Each of the ...' the subject is singular, so singular verb 'has completed' is required (agreement rule).

subject: English Language
text: By the time we reached the market, the stallholders ____ packing up.
explanation: Past perfect 'had already started' shows an action completed before another past action (sequence of past events).

subject: English Language
text: His report was concise and to the point; it showed great ____.
explanation: 'Concise' means brief and clear; 'conciseness' is the appropriate noun contrasting with verbosity or circumlocution.

subject: English Language
text: Which sentence uses the idiom 'cut his losses' correctly?
options: She cut his losses by investing more money to double the risk.
When the rain started, he cut his losses and carried on with the picnic.
The team cut his losses and tried to win every remaining match at all costs.
After months of fighting the lawsuit, he cut his losses and accepted the settlement.
explanation: 'Cut his losses' means to stop a losing activity to avoid further loss; option 0 uses it correctly in that sense.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correctly punctuated and capitalised sentence for reporting speech:
options: The director said, "We will start at nine."
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Correct form: lowercase 'director' after 'the', comma before quotation, and capital letter inside quotes for a full sentence.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has primary stress on the first syllable?
explanation: 'Photograph' has primary stress on the first syllable (PHO-to-graph). Others have stress on later syllables.

subject: English Language
text: A classmate asks, 'Could you lend me your notes for today?' Which is the most appropriate reply?
options: No, you must not read them.
Yes, I will send them after class.
explanation: Polite agreement to a request is appropriate: 'Yes, I will send them after class' offers help directly.

subject: English Language
text: Transform to passive: 'Farmers plant cassava every season.'
options: Cassava was planted by farmers every season.
Every season farmers are planting cassava.
Cassava will be planted by farmers every season.
Cassava is planted by farmers every season.
explanation: Present simple active becomes present simple passive: 'Cassava is planted by farmers' keeps habitual aspect intact.

subject: English Language
text: Kwame arrived ____ Lagos ____ noon for the cultural fair.
explanation: Use 'in' for cities and 'at' for specific times: 'in Lagos at noon' is the correct prepositional pair.

subject: English Language
text: Mariam smiled politely but remained silent when asked about the missing money. What is the most likely interpretation?
options: She admitted stealing the money openly.
She chose not to answer the sensitive question.
She laughed because she found the question funny.
explanation: A polite smile combined with silence most likely indicates a deliberate choice not to answer a sensitive question.

subject: English Language
text: None of the rice ____ acceptable for sale.
explanation: With the uncountable noun 'rice', 'none' takes a singular verb; use 'is' for present singular agreement.

subject: English Language
text: By the time the principal arrived, the invigilators ____ the question papers.
explanation: Past perfect ('had distributed') is used for an action completed before another past event (the principal's arrival).

subject: English Language
text: The teacher praised Aisha for her ____ in finishing the community health project.
explanation: 'Perseverance' means continued effort despite difficulty; other options are unrelated or contextually wrong here.

subject: English Language
text: Which sentence uses the idiom 'play it by ear' correctly?
options: He refused to play it by ear and insisted on learning the guitar.
We planned every detail, then decided to play it by ear.
She played it by ear, so she bought the tickets in advance.
After studying the map, they played it by ear to stay organized.
explanation: 'Play it by ear' means to improvise or decide as events unfold; sentence (a) correctly contrasts planning with choosing to improvise.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correctly punctuated and capitalised version of the sentence: Kweku said 'i will return by five'.
options: The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
Kweku said, 'I will return by five.'
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Direct speech needs a capital 'I' and a comma before the quotation when it follows a reporting verb: Kweku said, 'I will return by five.'.

subject: English Language
text: Which of these words has primary stress on the second syllable?
explanation: 'control' has primary stress on the second syllable (conTROL). The others ('TAblet', 'WINdow', 'MU-sic') have first-syllable stress.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has a different vowel sound from the others?
explanation: 'sheep' has the long vowel /iː/ while 'ship', 'sip', and 'chip' have the short /ɪ/ vowel; sheep is the odd one out.

subject: English Language
text: A guest asks, 'May I use your phone for a quick call?' Which is the most appropriate reply?
options: You will have to pay first.
Not unless you tell me why.
explanation: A polite, helpful response to a polite request is 'Yes, of course.' Other options are rude, irrelevant, or intrusive.

subject: English Language
text: Transform to passive: 'The committee will announce the results tomorrow.'
options: The results are announced by the committee tomorrow.
Tomorrow the committee will be announced the results.
The results will be announced by the committee tomorrow.
The results will announce by the committee tomorrow.
explanation: Correct passive form uses auxiliary 'will be' + past participle: 'The results will be announced by the committee tomorrow.'.

subject: English Language
text: After the rain stopped, the children ____ outside to play.
explanation: Use simple past ('went out') to describe a subsequent past action after 'stopped'; 'had gone out' is past perfect and not required for this sequence.

subject: English Language
text: Neither the headmaster nor the students ____ prepared for the surprise inspection.
explanation: With 'neither...nor' agreement follows the noun closest to the verb; 'students' is plural so use 'are'.

subject: English Language
text: By the time the convocation ceremony starts next year, I ____ my final project.
explanation: Use future perfect 'will have completed' to show an action finished before a future point in time.

subject: English Language
text: At the village meeting, the elders treated the newcomer with obvious ____.
explanation: 'Deference' means respectful submission or yielding to authority; other choices are unrelated meanings.

subject: English Language
text: Which sentence uses the idiom 'call it a day' correctly?
options: When the phone rang, he decided to call it a day and dialled his friend.
They told the crowd to call it a day meaning to shout loudly.
She called it a day by making a long telephone call.
After fixing the fence for hours, Sade said, 'Let's call it a day' and went inside.
explanation: 'Call it a day' idiomatically means to stop working for the day; option A uses it correctly, others use it literally or incorrectly.

subject: English Language
text: Correctly punctuate and capitalise this reporting of speech: aman: 'we will leave at dawn'.
options: Aman said, 'We will leave at dawn.'
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Proper nouns capitalised and quoted speech needs comma before the quote; sentence should read: Aman said, 'We will leave at dawn.'.

subject: English Language
text: In the word 'photograph' which syllable carries the primary stress?
explanation: 'Photograph' has primary stress on the first syllable: PHO-to-graph. Stress rule for this noun places stress on the first syllable.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has a different vowel sound from the others? ship, chip, sheep, sip
explanation: 'Sheep' has the long /iː/ vowel while 'ship','chip','sip' have the short /ɪ/ vowel; sheep is the odd one.

subject: English Language
text: A neighbour asks, 'Would you mind turning down the music?' Which reply is the most appropriate and polite?
explanation: To accept a polite request, respond positively and offer action: 'Yes, I'll turn it down.' is appropriate and courteous.

subject: English Language
text: Transform to passive: 'Asha had finished the report before the meeting began.'
options: The report had been finished by Asha before the meeting began.
The report was finished by Asha before the meeting had begun.
Asha had been finished the report before the meeting began.
Before the meeting began, the report finished by Asha had.
explanation: Past perfect passive requires 'had been' + past participle: 'The report had been finished by Asha...' is grammatically correct.

subject: English Language
text: During the drought the council rationed water; households received only one jerrycan per day. What is the most likely meaning of 'rationed' here?
explanation: 'Rationed' means to limit allocation and distribute sparingly, especially during shortages; other options do not match this control meaning.

subject: English Language
text: The list of names ____ on the noticeboard.
explanation: A noun phrase headed by 'list' is singular; use singular verb 'is'. Contrast with plural nouns which take 'are'.

subject: English Language
text: By 8 p.m. yesterday, they ____ the harvest.
explanation: Use past perfect ('had finished') for an action completed before a specific past time; simple past or present perfect are incorrect here.

subject: English Language
text: What is the closest meaning of 'meticulous' in 'Amina is meticulous about her notebook' ?
explanation: 'Meticulous' means very careful and thorough; it contrasts directly with 'careless' and not with 'ordinary' or 'quick'.

subject: English Language
text: Which sentence uses the idiom 'bite the bullet' correctly?
options: He bit the bullet every time he tasted the pepper.
After months of delay, she decided to bite the bullet and apologise.
They told him to bite the bullet to show no pain while eating.
She bit the bullet because the bread was hard.
explanation: 'Bite the bullet' means to accept an unpleasant action or decision; the first sentence shows this figurative meaning, others are literal or odd.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correctly punctuated and capitalised version of this reporting of speech: mr oku said 'we will return at noon'.
options: The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
Mr Oku said, 'We will return at noon'.
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Reporting verb needs a comma and the quoted sentence must begin with a capital letter: "Mr Oku said, 'We will return at noon.'" Other options mis-capitalise or omit the comma.

subject: English Language
text: In the word 'banana' which syllable carries the primary stress?
explanation: 'Banana' is stressed on the second syllable: ba-NA-na. This distinguishes it from words stressed on first or third syllables.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has a different vowel sound from the others: boat, throat, coat, book?
explanation: Boat, throat and coat share the /oʊ/ vowel sound; 'book' uses a different short vowel (/ʊ/), so it contrasts phonetically.

subject: English Language
text: A neighbour asks, 'Would you mind closing the gate when you leave?' Which is the most appropriate reply?
options: No, I mind. Close it yourself.
Not at all; I'll close it before I go.
I might close it later if I remember.
explanation: Polite acceptance to 'Would you mind...?' is phrased positively (e.g. 'Not at all; I'll...'). The other replies are rude, hesitant or refuse.

subject: English Language
text: Transform to passive: 'The committee chose Rebecca as chairperson.'
options: Rebecca is chosen as chairperson by the committee.
Was Rebecca chosen as chairperson by the committee?
Rebecca was chosen as chairperson by the committee.
The committee was chosen Rebecca as chairperson.
explanation: Active past simple ('chose') becomes passive 'was chosen'; the agent uses 'by the committee'. Other options misuse tense, form a question, or are ungrammatical.

subject: English Language
text: After the storm, the town faced a shortage of clean water. People queued at the borehole for hours. What is the most likely meaning of 'queued' here?
explanation: 'Queued' commonly means 'waited in line' (stood in order to be served). The context of a borehole and shortage supports this meaning, not dancing or arguing.

subject: English Language
text: Neither of the proposals ____ suitable for funding.
explanation: Use singular verb with 'neither of the ...': 'neither' treats the noun phrase as singular, so 'is' is correct.

subject: English Language
text: When I reached the lecture hall, the professor ____ the notes on the desk.
explanation: Past perfect (had left) shows the professor's action occurred before another past action (I reached), so 'had left' is required.

subject: English Language
text: The trek up the ridge was arduous.
explanation: 'Arduous' means difficult or tiring; 'exhausting' matches the sense, unlike 'easy', 'expensive' or 'short'.

subject: English Language
text: Which sentence uses the idiom 'beat around the bush' correctly?
options: She beat around the bush when she rescued the kitten.
He beat around the bush to mean he fixed the fence.
They beat around the bush to cook dinner early.
Stop beating around the bush and tell me the truth.
explanation: 'Beat around the bush' means avoid saying something directly; only the first sentence uses it idiomatically (asking for directness).

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correctly punctuated and capitalised version of this reported question: adjoa asked 'have you seen my umbrella'.
options: Adjoa asked, "Have you seen my umbrella?"
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Direct speech begins with a capital and is introduced by a comma; the question mark stays inside the quotes, so A is correct.

subject: English Language
text: In the word 'economy' which syllable carries the primary stress?
explanation: 'Economy' is stressed on the second syllable (e-CON-o-my); knowledge of common stress patterns confirms this placement.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has a different vowel sound from the others: coat, goat, bone, cough?
explanation: Coat, goat, bone share the /oʊ/ diphthong; 'cough' has a different vowel (/ɒ/ or /ɔ/), so it differs from the others.

subject: English Language
text: A colleague asks, 'Could you cover my shift on Friday?' Which is the most appropriate polite reply?
options: Why don't you ask someone else?
Sure, I can cover your shift on Friday.
explanation: A polite, helpful acceptance answers the request directly. 'Sure, I can cover...' is courteous and appropriate for that request.

subject: English Language
text: Transform to passive: 'The head gardener waters the seedlings every morning.'
options: The seedlings are watered by the head gardener every morning.
The head gardener is watered by the seedlings every morning.
The seedlings were watered by the head gardener every morning.
The seedlings are being watered by the head gardener every morning.
explanation: Present simple passive: plural 'seedlings' requires 'are watered' and agent is 'by the head gardener'; adverbial 'every morning' stays at end.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correct preposition: He is proficient ____ three programming languages.
explanation: The verb 'proficient' collocates with 'in' (proficient in a skill or subject); other prepositions are not standard with 'proficient'.
